content: 1. Every child has the right to access a comprehensive range of HIV-related services, ensuring their health and well-being. 2. Children are entitled to live in a safe environment, free from harm and exploitation, including protection from all forms of sexual abuse and exploitation. 3. They have the right to access accurate and appropriate health-related information, tailored to their specific needs and circumstances. 4. Children have the right to be free from disease and ill health, with access to preventive and curative measures. 5. The best interests of the child must guide all decisions and actions concerning their care and protection. 6. These rights apply universally to all children, regardless of their circumstances or behaviors, such as engaging in sex work or using injectable drugs. 7. Children are entitled to harm-reduction services and other interventions to prevent HIV and other infections, while also improving their overall health and well-being. 8. Services provided to adolescents must be developmentally appropriate, taking into account their cognitive and physical growth stages. 9. A continuum of care should adapt to the evolving capacities of adolescents, preparing them to manage their health and lives as they transition into adulthood. 10. Service providers must address the transitions adolescents face before and beyond adolescence, ensuring they are equipped to navigate adult health care systems. 11. A supportive legal and policy environment is essential for adolescents to access HIV testing, counseling, and linkage to appropriate treatment and care. 12. Criminalization of behaviors such as HIV transmission, same-sex relations, drug use, and commercial sexual exploitation significantly hinders adolescents' ability to access essential HIV-related services. 13. Adolescents who experience sexual exploitation or violence require referral to specialized child protection services, including legal and counseling support. 14. These services should include police and child protection units experienced in handling cases of sexual abuse and post-rape care. 15. Expanding access to HIV testing and counseling (HTC) for adolescents is critical to improving health outcomes and service uptake. 16. Operational questions remain on how to best deliver HTC services, link adolescents to care, and integrate lessons learned into existing systems with limited resources. 17. In South Africa, adolescents aged 12 and older can consent to HIV testing if they demonstrate sufficient maturity to understand the benefits, risks, and implications of the test. 18. This policy reflects efforts to lower barriers to health care access for younger adolescents, recognizing their autonomy and the need for early intervention. 19. Linking HIV testing to prevention, treatment, and care is vital. Adolescents, particularly those at high risk, must receive adequate post-test counseling and support. 20. Counseling prior to testing plays a crucial role in encouraging adolescents to access services and adhere to care plans. 21. Group-based counseling programs, such as South Africa's Hlanganani, have shown promise in helping newly diagnosed adolescents link to care and initiate antiretroviral therapy (ART). 22. These programs provide a supportive environment for adolescents to share experiences and build life skills, improving adherence and retention in care. 23. Innovative approaches, such as using TV, radio, mobile phones, and social media, are being employed to engage adolescents in sub-Saharan Africa and improve their access to HIV services. 24. Despite progress, challenges remain, including stigma, fear of disclosure, and logistical barriers to service delivery. 25. Adolescents living with HIV (ALHIV) require tailored sexual and reproductive health (ASRH) services that emphasize disclosure, self-esteem, and responsible sexual health practices. 26. Programs must address the unique challenges faced by ALHIV, such as balancing positive living with sexual needs and navigating disclosure to potential partners. 27. Support programs like Jamaica's Eve for Life provide comprehensive care for adolescent mothers living with HIV, focusing on adherence, disclosure, and emotional well-being. 28. These programs recruit vulnerable adolescents through antenatal or HIV treatment services and assess their needs to provide targeted support. 29. Support groups offer a safe space for adolescents to discuss challenges, share successes, and build life skills, free from stigma and discrimination. 30. A team-based approach to adherence support ensures that adolescents receive consistent care and guidance, fostering trust and improving outcomes.
